tools.name: accept_role_message
tools.description:
Accept a claimed delivery: commits a permanent receipt. {disposition.kind} is 'work' (you will do the work, then ack_role_message) or 'no_work' (acceptance records why no work was spawned). Role work lives in this receipt and ack_role_message; it is not mirrored into wv_queue. Idempotent on same (delivery, instance, generation, kind) — a replay returns the same receiptId; a different kind returns status='conflict'. Returns {receiptId}.
Docs: arc-f-inboxes-and-triage/index.html

kind.description:
`"work"` records that the acceptor will do the work (then
`ack_role_message`); `"no_work"` records the `noteOrReason` and spawns
no work. Neither value writes a `wv_queue` row — role work lives only
in the acceptance receipt.

team.description:
The `(org, team)` the role mailbox lives in. The viewer-visible
team identity, mirroring `InboxTeam`.

tools.name: ack_role_message
tools.description:
Acknowledge a delivery previously accepted by this instance. Pass the {receiptId} accept_role_message returned. Idempotent: a re-ack with the same receiptId succeeds. A different receiptId or a stale (expired / released) claim fails with StaleAck. Returns {}. Acknowledgement is distinct from completing the underlying work — a work item in wv_queue remains governed by the queue state machine.
Docs: arc-f-inboxes-and-triage/index.html

team.description:
The `(org, team)` the role mailbox lives in. The viewer-visible
team identity, mirroring `InboxTeam`.

tools.name: add_source_repo
tools.description:
Add a source repo to a team. Pass `org` (owner/repo) and `team`, plus exactly one of `url` (a remote — https://…, git@…, host/owner/repo, or GitHub shorthand owner/repo — tracked on the team) or `path` (the absolute path of a folder on this machine, which is then bound as the repo's local clone). A folder is tracked as the repo its `upstream` remote names when it has one (the canonical repo in a fork workflow), else its `origin`, else `local/<folder>`; the result's `remoteName` says which remote was used. A folder inside a git repository must be that repository's root. CodeSense never clones: clone with git yourself, then pass `path` (or add by `url` and bind the clone later with attach_source_repo_path). Returns { status:"ok", data:{ owner, repo, provider, host, remoteKey, localPath, remoteName, remoteUrl } }; an unknown or archived team returns { status:"unauthorizedTeam" }; a bad URL or folder, a duplicate, or invalid source identity returns { status:"validation", message }.
Docs: arc-l-factory/team-and-notes-tools.html

path.description:
An absolute path to a folder on this machine: tracked as the repo its
git `origin` names (`local/<folder>` without one) and bound as that
repo's local clone. Pass this or `url`, not both.

team.description: The team to add the repo to.

url.description:
A remote to track: `https://…`, `git@…`, `host/owner/repo`, or GitHub
shorthand `owner/repo`. Pass this or `path`, not both.

tools.name: agent_list
tools.description:
List every agent you can see: your Only-me agents (private, per-org), team agents on teams synced on this Mac, and the shipped starters — `builtin/claude`, `builtin/codex` (each runtime's defaults with your own CLI login), and their `*-unattended` twins (permission checks skipped — what a background launch naming no agent runs). Starters are read-only (copy one to customize). Optional: {scope} `all` (default) | `mine` | `team` | `builtin` (view filter, not permission). {includeArchived} default false. {includeManifest} default false — resolves each agent's startup manifest (reads every startup file). Returns `{ok:true, data:[{id, name, description, runtime, launch, mcp_servers, startup_count, created_by, scope, org, team, archived, revision, manifest?:{files, bytes, error_count}}]}`. `id` is what every agent_* tool takes; `revision` is agent_update's `baseRevision`. To fork any listed agent ("Copy to Mine"), including a starter: agent_get it, then agent_create its `definition` with `scope:"personal"` + the `org`. Spend fields include budgetUsd {perDay?, perWeek?}, budgetPending, and spend {today, week, state: ok|warn|reached|unpriced}; spend counts all machines on this core.
Docs: arc-e-agents/agent-design.html

includeManifest.description:
Resolve each agent's startup manifest and add its `{files, bytes,
error_count}`. Default false: it reads every startup file.

scope.description:
`all` (default), `mine` (your Only me agents and the team agents you
created), `team` (team agents only) or `builtin` (the read-only starter
agents CodeSense ships: `builtin/claude`, `builtin/codex`, their unattended twins
`builtin/claude-unattended` and `builtin/codex-unattended`).

tools.name: archive_team
tools.description:
Archive (`archived:true`) or unarchive (`archived:false`) a team — org-wide, reversible retirement, the same edit as the UI's Archive. An archived active team is switched off in the UI. Pass `org`, `team`, `archived`. Returns { status:"ok", data:{ orgSlug, edit:"ArchiveTeam", team } }; an unknown team returns { status:"validation", message }.
Docs: arc-l-factory/team-and-notes-tools.html

team.description: The team to archive or unarchive.

tools.name: attach_context_repository
tools.description:
Attach an existing local context checkout in place. No provider account, remote URL or active team required. Never copies files or runs Git transport. Paths are on this Mac.
Docs: arc-b-model/orgs.html

clonePath.description: Absolute path to the existing checkout on the local desktop.

tools.name: attach_source_repo_path
tools.description:
Bind (or rebind) a local clone to one of a team's source repos, so worktrees, terminals and editor actions find its code. Pass `org`, `team`, `repo` (owner/repo, or host/owner/repo when the same owner/repo is on two forges) and `path` — the absolute path of a git working tree's root with a remote that names that repo. Remotes are tried `origin`, then `upstream`, then the rest, so a fork whose `upstream` is the team's repo binds; the result's `remoteName` says which remote matched. A folder that is not a working-tree root (the error names the root to pick), has no remote, or has no remote naming the repo is refused. Rebinding replaces the previous clone. CodeSense never clones: clone with git first. Returns { status:"ok", data:{ owner, repo, provider, host, remoteKey, localPath, remoteName, remoteUrl } }; an unknown team returns { status:"unauthorizedTeam" }; a repo the team does not track or a bad clone returns { status:"validation", message }.
Docs: arc-l-factory/team-and-notes-tools.html

path.description: Absolute path to a git working tree whose `origin` is `repo`.

repo.description:
One of the team's source repos: `owner/repo`, or `host/owner/repo`
when the same `owner/repo` is on two forges.

tools.name: claim_role_messages
tools.description:
Take messages from a role's queue so no other holder works them. Args: {team} `{org, team}`, {role}, {instanceId} and {generation} exactly as register_role returned them; {limit} optional, 1-50, default 50. Returns {deliveries: [{deliveryId, messageId, role, claimToken, claimExpiresAt, text, from, createdAtMs, existingReceipt?}]}, oldest first; an empty list means the queue is empty. text/from/createdAtMs are the message itself (createdAtMs epoch ms), so no second read is needed. claimToken is this claim's proof: pass it to accept_role_message, then ack_role_message. claimExpiresAt is epoch seconds; while your session runs (registered with sessionId) CodeSense keeps your claims alive with your registration, otherwise accept and ack before it or the message returns to the queue. existingReceipt {receiptId, kind, queueItemId}, when present, means an earlier holder already accepted this message: do not accept again, finish the work and ack_role_message with that receiptId. queueItemId is deprecated and always null for new receipts — role work is not mirrored into wv_queue. Reading the inbox never claims; only this verb does, in one atomic step. Fails with 'registration is stale or expired' when your registration lapsed or the generation is wrong: call register_role again and use the generation it returns. Next: accept_role_message.
Docs: arc-f-inboxes-and-triage/index.html

limit.description: Up to 50. Omit for the default (50).

team.description:
The `(org, team)` the role mailbox lives in. The viewer-visible
team identity, mirroring `InboxTeam`.

tools.name: codesense_overview
tools.description:
Overview of CodeSense right now, in ONE read-only call: start here to answer any question about CodeSense state. Returns { generatedAt, context (active org/team), machines (connection status), sessions (running agents/terminals by state and machine, who launched whom, who needs you), agents (saved Agents), routines (enabled, last run, needs you), inbox (human unread; sessions with unread mail), roleQueues (per role in the active team: pending/claimed/accepted deliveries and live instances), workspaces (open workspaces and their tabs), docs (where the bundled CodeSense docs and the concepts guide are) }. Each section has `detail`: the tools to call for the full data. A section that could not be read has `error` instead of data; the rest still answer. Lists are capped (`truncated: true` when cut). Optional {guide: true}: return the concepts guide instead (how CodeSense works: orgs, teams, content layers, workspaces, machines, sessions, Agents, roles, inboxes, routines, notes, dashboards, each with its MCP tools).
Docs: arc-a-first-touch/identity-menu-and-switcher.html

guide.description:
Return the concepts guide (how CodeSense works, with the tool for each concept)
instead of the state overview. Default false.

tools.name: create_local_organization
tools.description:
Create and attach a local organization in a NEW absolute destinationPath under an existing parent. displayName defines its stable local identity. Uses canonical empty registries and unborn Git main; no account, active team, remote, credentials or commit. Existing folders and duplicate identities are refused. Paths are on this Mac. Returns the loaded organization and created outcome. If registration fails, the error names the preserved folder for Attach context repository retry.
Docs: arc-b-model/orgs.html

destinationPath.description: Absolute NEW folder beneath an existing parent. Existing folders are refused.

displayName.description: Nonempty organization name; identity becomes local/<sanitized-name>.

tools.name: create_team
tools.description:
Create a team in an org — the same edit as the UI's New team. Pass `org` (owner/repo) and `name` (a lowercase slug); optional `parent` nests it under an existing team (checked first, so a bad parent creates nothing), and `activate:true` then switches the app to it exactly as set_active_team does. You are recorded as the creator. The UI shows the new team without a reload. Returns { status:"ok", data:{ orgSlug, edit:"CreateTeam", team, activated, activationError?, warnings? } }; warnings appears only when `parent` has no config/sharing.yml and so shares nothing with the new team. If the switch fails the team stays created with activated:false and activationError saying why; an invalid, reserved or duplicate name or a bad parent returns { status:"validation", message } with the registry's reason and writes nothing.
Docs: arc-l-factory/team-and-notes-tools.html

activate.description: Also switch the app to the new team, as `set_active_team` does.

org.description: The context-repo org slug (`owner/repo`) to create the team in.

parent.description: An existing team to nest the new team under.

tools.name: delete_team
tools.description:
Delete a team from an org's registry — the same edit as the UI's Delete team. Only the registry entry is removed; the team's content stays on disk (git-recoverable). If it was the active team the UI falls back to another team. Pass `org`, `team`. Returns { status:"ok", data:{ orgSlug, edit:"DeleteTeam", team } }; an unknown team returns { status:"validation", message }.
Docs: arc-l-factory/team-and-notes-tools.html

team.description: The team to remove from the org's registry.

tools.name: describe_setup
tools.description:
Setup checklist. No arguments. The first attribution replacement notice is acknowledged in its diagnostic receipt. Returns `{status:"ok", data:{activeOrg, activeTeam, orgs:[...], scratch:{orgs:[...], allOrgs}, attribution:{status, binary, gitAiVersion, daemonReachable, supportedVersions, previousBinary, warnings, capture, notesRef, notesPushRepos, daemonRepoRoots}}}`. `attribution` is the machine's line-attribution doctor: whether the exact bundled git-ai pin at ~/.codesense/bin/git-ai is installed and its managed daemon answers (`supportedVersions` names the accepted pin; `status.kind` active | off with reason | installing | install_failed with message | not_installed | unsupported_version with found | unsupported with reason | error with message). A PATH copy is never run; `warnings` reports user_copy_present, user_hooks_present, replacement and install-failure messages, or restart pending. Old or restored copies keep capture off; a restored copy reports unsupported with reason user_pinned. To reinstall, call save_source_repo_attachment with {repoPath: absolute checkout path, attribution: on}. `previousBinary` is null or {version,replacement,path}, persisted across restarts; a pending replacement warning survives restart and is shown once. Install failures stay readable until a successful retry; app restart retries them. `capture` reports the last completed startup or watcher checkpoint pass: {lastSweepAt (epoch ms or null), trigger (startup|watcher or null), clonesSwept, logsSeen, logsNew, traceRowsStored, sessionMappingRowsStored, watchErrors, lastError}. It is retained per CodeSense home in memory since app start; reads never trigger a sweep. watchErrors counts registration failures in the latest watch reconciliation. Counts cover that pass; logsNew means first-imported files, and sessionMappingRowsStored counts stored rows carrying an s_ identity. A repo's own setting can still keep a worktree off (save_source_repo_attachment `attribution`: on|off|auto). Notes stay on this Mac in refs/notes/sense (`notesRef`) unless a repo is set `notes`: push; `notesPushRepos` lists those repos. `daemonRepoRoots` counts the attached clones CodeSense lists in git-ai's daemon_repo_roots, so its daemon ignores other repos (0: no list, so every repo; null while no attached clone resolves and the list written before is kept), and a worktree of an unattached repo launches off with reason repo_not_attached until its clone is attached. Each org has `{slug, displayName, orgRoot, remoteUrl, loadErrors?, teams:[...]}`; each team has `{name, archived, parent?, starterPage?, synced, sourceRepos:[{repo, status, localPath}]}` (`starterPage`: the declared file the team opens when nothing is open, relative to its content folder; absent ⇒ README.md / README.html / index.html) where `status` is `attached` (bound to an existing checkout), `missing` (bound but the checkout is gone), or `unattached` (no checkout recorded). `scratch` is your private space (never shared), one local git repo at `scratch.repo.path`, never pushed; uncommitted counts edits no commit holds yet. Use set_viewer_state navLens source private to show it, and set_private_items_use to change a team switch. Per-org: `{counts:{notes, overlayFiles, panes, routines, agents}, offTeams, settingsDamaged}` applies only in that org; `scratch.allOrgs:{skills, prompts, snippets, templates, notApplied}` are inert files that apply across every org. Use the result to decide the next tool: create_team/set_active_team, attach_source_repo_path (for `unattached`/`missing`; never add_source_repo for an already-tracked repo), agent_list → agent_create, routine_create.
Docs: arc-b-model/orgs.html

tools.name: detach_context_repository
tools.description:
Unregister a local context checkout by orgSlug. Never deletes or modifies checkout files. Works for unavailable roots. Paths are on this Mac.
Docs: arc-b-model/orgs.html

tools.name: get_story_format
tools.description:
Authoring entry point. Returns the decision-first contract for creating CodeSense content: whether you need frontmatter at all (most content is a plain doc and needs none), the full pipeline-story frontmatter schema (Markdown + HTML `cs:*` forms, with the closed `type`/`status` enums), the validate_story finding codes, and cross-refs to list_source_repos + validate_story. Call this first.
Docs: arc-h-pipelines-and-sdlc/runs-and-stories.html

tools.name: inbox_list
tools.description:
List inbox messages WITHOUT marking anything read (read_messages is the one that drains your own unread mail). Every agent session, every role (any role name, usually a saved Agent's id) and the human (`human`) has an inbox in each team. Args, all optional: {scope} `to-human` (messages to the human), `to-agents` (to sessions and roles) or `all` — default `to-human` with no filter, `all` with one; {agentId} (a saved Agent id from agent_list: its role inbox, the inboxes of the sessions running it, and every reply under them); {sessionId} (a list_sessions handle or a session id: what that session sent and received, and the replies; pass your own $CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID for your own history); {role} (messages to and from that role queue); {limit} (newest N; default 50, at most 500); {before} (a messageId: only older ones; to page, pass the last listed messageId while hasMore); {include} ["text"] for every body in full (else a body over 2 KB comes as textPreview, its first 512 bytes, with truncated:true) and ["conversations"] for the human's conversation summaries; {kind} `needs-you` | `update` (only messages of that kind, applied before {limit}; kind marks whether mail waits on the human for agent views and dashboards); {team} `{org, team}` (default: the {sessionId}'s team, else the team active in the app). Returns {messages, humanUnread, hasMore, total (messages that matched, older than before when given, ahead of limit)}; an answer stays under 64 KB, so older messages past that wait for the next page; conversations are opt-in: include:["conversations"]. `messages` is newest first: [{messageId, from, fromName, to, toName, text (or textPreview and truncated), createdAtMs, inReplyTo, inReplyToTeam, toHuman, unread, primaryFile?, archivedAtMs?, delivery, onClick?, contentType?, replyTo?, replyToName?, summary?, replyTargetEnded, via?, kind}]. `kind`: `needs-you` (waits on the human) or `update` (informational); the human Inbox shows both in conversations and counts all unread human mail, so on a message to a session or role (scope `to-agents`/`all`) it is just what the sender set — text typed into a terminal is always `update`; else the kind its sender set; else `needs-you` when it carries a `replyTo` naming someone other than the human, its sender or a role its sender holds; else `update`. `via`: `terminal` for text typed into the recipient's terminal with send_to_session (it already has it: stored read, never returned by read_messages); absent for mail. `summary`: the sender's one-line plain-text preview (show it instead of `text` in a list; absent when the sender gave none). `replyTo`: where replies to it go instead of its sender (a session handle, `human`, or `role:<id>`); `replyToName` its display name. `replyTargetEnded`: a reply would go to a session that is no longer running (it waits unread in that inbox; send to a role instead). `from`/`to` are session handles, role ids or `human`; `fromName`/`toName` their display names. `createdAtMs`/`archivedAtMs` are epoch milliseconds. `unread`: the recipient has not read it yet. `inReplyTo`: the messageId it answers (thread link). `primaryFile`: an attached team-content path. `onClick`: `{type: goto-agent|open-file|show-message}`. `contentType`: plain | markdown (default) | html. `delivery` (role messages and withdrawn ones; else null): {state, pickedUpAtMs, instance, acceptedAtMs, disposition (work|no_work), note, withdrawnAtMs} where state is `queued` (no instance holds it), `reading` (claimed), `accepted`, `done` (acknowledged) or `withdrawn`. `humanUnread` counts unread messages to the human in the whole team inbox, of both kinds. Next: answer one with reply {messageId}; see a role's queue and who holds it with role_state; see who runs with list_sessions.
Docs: arc-f-inboxes-and-triage/messages.html

agentId.description:
A saved Agent's id (`agent_list`): its role inbox, the inboxes of its running
instances, and every reply under them.

before.description:
A messageId: only messages older than it. To page, pass the last listed messageId
while `hasMore`.

include.description: `text`: every body in full; `conversations`: the human's conversation summaries.

items.description: What an agent's `inbox_list` asks for beyond the bounded default.

oneOf.description: Every body in full, however long.

anyOf.description:
What a message asks of the human, for agent views and dashboards. The human
inbox shows both kinds as conversations and counts all unread human mail. Stored as given on `wv_inbox.kind` (NULL when the sender set none); reads
resolve the effective kind with [`InboxMessage::effective_kind`].

oneOf.description: Waits on the human: a question, a decision, something only they can unblock.

kind.description:
Only messages of this effective kind: `needs-you` (waits on the human) or
`update` (informational). Applied before `limit`.

limit.description:
At most this many messages, newest first: at most 500 (the inbox keeps the newest
500); an agent's `inbox_list` lists 50 when it names none, a page's `inbox()` 500.

role.description: A role (any role name, usually a saved Agent's id): messages to and from it, and replies.

scope.description:
`to-human` (messages to the human), `to-agents` (messages to sessions and
roles) or `all`. Default: `to-human` with no filter below, `all` with one.

sessionId.description:
A session (a `list_sessions` handle or a session id): what it sent and received,
and every reply under them.

anyOf.description:
The `(org, team)` the role mailbox lives in. The viewer-visible
team identity, mirroring `InboxTeam`.

team.description:
The team `{org, team}`; default: the `sessionId`'s team, else the team active
in the app.

tools.name: inbox_post
tools.description:
Post an item to the Inbox ("I need you"). The dead-simple outbound primitive: An agent with a verified CodeSense tab connection calls this to call a human back (an unbound CLI or trigger is refused; start it in a CodeSense terminal) — it appears on the ONE universal Inbox next to CodeSense-native items. Inputs: `title` (REQUIRED, non-blank — the headline the human lands on), optional `context` (folded into the item's sentence), optional `backlink` (a link back to the run/subject), and `need` — one of `awaiting-answer` | `needs-approval` | `needs-attention` | `awaiting-validation` | `done` (defaults to `needs-attention`) so the Inbox maps need → the matching action. This SHOWS a pending item; it does NOT gate a run. Returns {id}.
Docs: arc-f-inboxes-and-triage/messages.html

backlink.description:
Optional backlink to the run / subject this post is about (an opaque routing
ref the Inbox row links back to). Scrubbed + bounded.

context.description:
Optional extra context, folded into the item's one-sentence summary after the
title. Scrubbed + bounded.

need.description:
The DECLARED need — one of `awaiting-answer` | `needs-approval` |
`needs-attention` | `awaiting-validation` | `done`. Defaults to
`needs-attention` when omitted, so every posted item carries a need.

title.description: The headline the human lands on — REQUIRED, non-blank. Scrubbed + bounded.

tools.name: list_machines
tools.description:
List the machines an org/team sees, as the Machines panel lists them: This Mac first, then the team's shared machines, then your private ones. Required: `orgSlug`. Optional: `team` (include that team's shared machines; describe_setup lists orgs and teams). Returns `[{machineId, kind, label, scope, declaration, binding, canPublish, status, attention, capabilities, remoteMcpControl?, terminalServer?, load1?, cpuCount?, memUsedBytes?, memTotalBytes?, diskFreeBytes?, diskTotalBytes?, diskPath?, sampledAt?, machineStatsSupported?}]`. `machineId` is what open_workspace {machineId} and open_remote_tab take (`local` = This Mac). `kind`: `local` | `ssh`. `scope`: null for This Mac, `{kind:"personal"}`, or `{kind:"team", orgSlug, team}`. `declaration` (null for This Mac): the shareable half — `{host, port, jumpHost, defaultBaseDir, pinnedHostKeyFp, pinnedServerId}`; `binding`: your own connection settings for it, null when you never connected. `status.state`: `connected` (with `workspaces`, the open workspace count), `idle`, `connecting`, `handshaking`, `reconnecting` (`attempt`), `disconnected`, `unreachable` (`lastReachedAtMs`, `retryInSecs`), `connectionFailed` (`lastError`), `needsCredential`, `authFailed` (`reason`), `hostKeyChanged`, `notInstalled` (its terminal server is not installed), `versionMismatch`, `terminalServerFrozen`. `attention`: how many agents there wait on you. `capabilities.agentCallbacks`: whether agents launched there can reach this app's MCP (inbox, roles, progress, hooks): true only for a set-up private-account machine with remote MCP control on (set_machine_remote_mcp_control); a team-shared machine has none. `terminalServer` (connected machines only; absent otherwise): the running terminal server next to this app — `{serverVersion?` (the app release it was built for; absent for an older build that predates build stamps), `appVersion`, `upToDate`, `relation` (`same` | `older` | `newer` | `otherBuild`: This Mac's server belongs to another CodeSense build sharing this Mac — `upToDate` is false, but only `older` servers are out of date and offered the update), `announcedVersion`, `buildCommit?`, `builtAtMs?`, `buildDigest?`, `devBuild`, and for This Mac `serverPath`, `appServerPath` (the server this app ships), `startedAtMs`, `pid}`. A remote machine whose server is `older` also has `status.terminalServerUpdate: true`, and after connect_machine or retry_machine `status.terminalServerSessions` (the sessions an update ends; a list leaves it out). Resources are optional self-reported terminal-server observations: `load1` is the 1-minute load average, `cpuCount` logical cores; memory and disk are bytes, memory used is total minus available, disk is the volume holding the server workspace directory labelled by `diskPath`, and `sampledAt` is Unix epoch milliseconds on the server. A call reuses a sample under 30 seconds old or takes one one-shot sample without subscribing. An older server has `machineStatsSupported: false` and no resource fields: unknown (update the terminal server). Disconnected rows omit these fields. Samples are local runtime state, never synced or a reservation; re-check before depending on free disk. The visible Machines tab receives a 30-second stream through the machineStats LiveHub topic; it stops watching when hidden. No secrets are returned. A dashboard's codesense.machines() returns the same list for the page's team.
Docs: arc-d-terminals-and-machines/index.html

tools.name: list_orgs_teams
tools.description:
List the signed-in user's orgs and teams: the discovery surface for targeting team-scoped tools at a specific team. Returns { org, team, synced, starterPage? } entries (`starterPage`: the team's declared starter page, relative to its content folder) bounded to the user's LOCALLY-SYNCED memberships (not all teams). No arguments. Use the org/team you find here as the optional `org`/`team` args on other team-scoped tools; omit them to use the active team.
Docs: arc-b-model/orgs.html

tools.name: list_sessions
tools.description:
List every session CodeSense is running — local + remote. Returns `{sessions: [{handle, displayName, state, sessionId, effectiveStatus, crashId?, needsYouKind?, launchedBy, unread, oldestUnreadAt, mailNotice, notifiedAt, inboxWaiter, subagents?, story?, workspace?, machine?, machineId?, workspaceHandle?, role?, avatar?, agent?, progress?, launchTelemetry?, deadlineAtMs?, expiring?}]}`. `effectiveStatus` is the sessions projection's display status; `crashId`, when present, names the current crash/failure mark for dismiss_agent_mark. `needsYouKind`, when set, says why it needs you (`startup`: stuck on a startup screen). `deadlineAtMs` is the epoch-ms deadline of a bounded local launch (`open_workspace`'s `maxRuntime`), pushed later while a person types in its pane; absent for unbounded or remote rows. The row goes once the sweep's kill releases it. `expiring: true` marks the ~30s grace between the sweep's `/exit` and its kill; absent otherwise. `progress` is its latest signal_progress: `{phase, step?, total?, note?, atMs}`, phase as in signal_progress, `step` of `total`, `atMs` epoch ms; kept while the app runs. `launchTelemetry` is the saved-agent launch's record, present once finalized: `{sessionId, agent, launchMode: "shell"|"argv", metricsVersion, startedAtMs, ptyFirstByteMs?, settleMs?, injectedAtMs?, agentLiveMs?, outcome: "succeeded"|"settle_timeout"|"wait_live_elapsed"|"spawn_failed"|"canceled", errorText?, binaryPath?, binaryVersion?} — `binaryPath`/`binaryVersion` are present when the launch resolved the agent CLI (metricsVersion 3+); the shell-only `settleMs`, `injectedAtMs` are null on argv launches; absent on older sessions. `releaseQualified: false` (+`releaseNote`): its CLI release is unqualified; status, wake and usage may fail. Else absent. `agent` is the saved Agent it runs (an agent_list id; agent_get shows it with all its running instances); `role` and `avatar` are display labels its launcher gave it, not a role inbox. `state`: `running` | `idle` (turn finished) | `needs-you` (a real permission prompt, an open ask_user question, or blocked progress; never a completed needs-attention outcome) | `exited` | `offline` (machine disconnected; may still run there) | `unknown` (no observation). `subagents` counts its running subagents (absent at none); `state` stays the agent's own, so a finished turn with subagents working is `idle` with `subagents: N`, and mail reaches it as for any idle agent. `displayName` is the live tab name. `machine` is "This Mac" for local tabs; `launchedBy` is the launcher handle or null for human-launched. `unread` is this session's unread inbox count (same as read_messages with its session id; role-inbox mail excluded; null when the team is not synced here); `oldestUnreadAt` is the RFC-3339 timestamp of the oldest unread, or null when unread is 0. `mailNotice` says whether its inbox notice told the agent about that unread mail: `told` (all of it; told is not read; the agent decides when), `pending` (newer mail not announced yet), null with none unread; `notifiedAt` is when it was last told (RFC 3339) or null. `inboxWaiter` is true when new mail reaches the agent at once (an idle agent starts a turn, a running one hears at its next step or turn); false when CodeSense cannot tell it (no CLI wake path, an unnamed process, or a gone waiter), so its mail stays held. An idle Claude with a dead waiter may be recovered with a one-line inbox notice only when its input box is empty and nobody is typing; otherwise wake it with send_to_session telling it to call read_messages. A supported CLI can be inbox-ready before its first prompt once its engine and trusted observers establish readiness; startup menus, approvals and unavailable engines keep it unready. `inboxWaiter` is "unknown" for a tab on a machine that is not connected now (its waiter may still be waiting there). Listing marks nothing read (inbox_list {sessionId: handle} peeks). Optional {launched_by} filters to sessions that launcher started.
Docs: arc-c-workspaces-and-worktrees/workspace-and-tab-lifecycle.html

launched_by.description: A session id or handle: list only the sessions it launched.

tools.name: list_source_repos
tools.description:
List legal legacy `source_repo` values plus structured canonical repository identities. `primary`/`byTeam` omit host-ambiguous owner/repo values; use `sourceRepoIdentities` for explicit provider, host, and remoteKey details, plus each repo's local clone: `attachment` (`attached` = bound to a checkout that exists, `missing` = bound but the checkout is gone, `unattached` = none) and `localPath`. Never invent a source_repo; resolve it here.
Docs: arc-h-pipelines-and-sdlc/runs-and-stories.html

tools.name: open_workspace
tools.description:
Open a story workspace and return its handle (the story_id — pass back as an abstract address, never a raw PTY id). Creates the managed worktree on first open (no context is copied until an agent launches there or calls hydrate_worktree/hydrate_story). Args: {story_id} (e.g. "DEMO-1"; unknown/non-managed id is refused). Optional: {mode} `headed` (default; visible + focused) | `visible-unfocused` | `headless` (background agent, opt-in); {initial_prompt} (the agent's starting prompt — a slash command works). Returns `{handle, mode, headed, reconciled}` (reconciled: `{from,to}` when the story's `branch` frontmatter differs from the opened branch, else null; this call does not write the story doc). Drive with send_to_session. Gated by the Interactive tier (refuses `not-granted:`/`denied:`/`busy`).

LAUNCH AN AGENT: pass {target} `story` (with {story_id}; add {name} to open a new tab in that worktree — handle `<storyId>#<name>`; name is lowered + dash-normalized, max 64) or `team-workspace` (with {name}; a context worktree of the team's context repo, on its own branch, with CWD <team>/content. Pick an existing one by {worktree} id or name from list_worktrees {kind:context, team}, or create one with {worktree, createWorktree:true}. Pass {worktree} whenever the user named one. Omit both to reuse the most recently used, or create one named after {name} when none exists. Several agents share a worktree as tabs; reopening is the same call. Result adds worktree:{id,name,branch,created}; tell the user where it landed). Optional: {team} (defaults to your own team for agent sessions, or the active team when a person calls it; with `story`, a team other than the story's is refused), {org} (defaults to your own org; a person's story is found by id, and an id in several orgs needs org), {agent} (an agent id from agent_list; default `builtin/claude`, or `builtin/claude-unattended` for headless), {initial_prompt}, {launched_by} (your $CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID; omit for human-launched), {queue_role} (queue id; omitted inherits the saved agent default; null joins no queue), {role} (display label; a story launch whose role or saved agent is a reviewer gets a `type: review` task with `typeSource`), {reviews} (story target only: the dev task id the reviewer reviews, linked `relates_to:reviews` exactly; omitted, the story's latest open task, `associated`), {avatar} (display only: `pack:id` from avatar_list, a `#rrggbb`, or an emoji), {max_runtime} (how long the launched session may run, like `30m` or `2h`, range 1m–24h; when it is reached the agent is sent `/exit`, then killed 30s later, and the launcher is notified; while a person types in the session's pane the deadline moves to at least 15 minutes after their last keystroke, so a session someone is using is not stopped; absent = no limit; This Mac only). Returns `{status:"opened"|"alreadyLive"|"busy"|"invalid", handle, name, message, warnings?}`. On `alreadyLive` with `maxRuntime`, the existing deadline (or lack of one) is left unchanged and the result carries a `maxRuntime ignored: session already live` warning.

ON A MACHINE: pass {story_id} + {machine_id} (from list_machines; "local" = this Mac). First open on a new machine copies the local clone there (no GitHub creds needed). To launch an agent there, add {target} `story` + {name}/{agent}/{initial_prompt}. A story whose workspace lives elsewhere is refused. With {machine_id} the call returns once the workspace is open there (status `opened`), or fails with the reason; it waits up to 10 minutes, then fails as `unconfirmed`. Team-workspace targets run on this Mac only; machine launches are never headless. {max_runtime} + a non-local {machine_id} is refused `invalid` (enforcement is This Mac only; follow-up for remote). Identity comes from the verified MCP connection; an unbound caller is refused. A supplied launched_by must name the caller itself. Omitted team selects the agent session's own team; human calls use the active team. A child agent cannot open a workspace on a shared parent story; a human can.
Docs: arc-c-workspaces-and-worktrees/index.html

agent.description:
The agent to launch (with `target`): its key, or a bare id found in the target
team, then your private space, then the starters. Defaults to `builtin/claude`, or
`builtin/claude-unattended` for a headless open.

avatar.description:
The face to show for the session: `pack:id` (see `avatar_list`), or a colour or
emoji hint. Display only; a face whose pack is not on this machine falls back.

createWorktree.description: Create worktree as a new name; refuse an existing name.

headed.description:
Legacy visibility toggle, kept for back-compat. Prefer
`mode`. When `mode` is absent: `Some(false)` → background (headless),
`Some(true)`/`None` → headed (visible + focused). `mode` wins when both set.

initial_prompt.description: Optional first prompt seeded into the spawned agent (e.g. "/review").

launched_by.description:
Who is launching: your `$CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID`. Omit when a person asked.
Shown as "Launched by"; nothing is checked against it.

machine_id.description:
Open the story's workspace on this machine (an id from `list_machines`, or
`local` for This Mac) instead of This Mac. Its worktree is created there on
first open; later opens reuse it. With `target: "story"` the agent launches
there; a team-workspace target runs on This Mac only.

max_runtime.description:
how long the launched session may run, like `30m` or `2h`
(range 1m–24h). When it is reached the agent is sent `/exit`, then killed
30s later, and the launcher is notified. Absent/blank: no limit. This Mac
only — combining it with a non-local `machineId` is refused.

mode.description:
How the workspace surfaces — `"headed"` (visible + focused, the
default) · `"visible-unfocused"` (a real tab that does not steal focus) ·
`"headless"` (background; opt-in only). Absent → resolved from `headed`
(default headed). An unrecognized value is refused `denied:`.

org.description: The org of the story or team. Defaults to your own org for agent sessions. For a person, the story's org is found by id, and an id in more than one org needs `org`.

queue_role.description: Team queue id; omitted inherits saved default, null joins no queue.

reviews.description:
The task a reviewer launch reviews (a task id from `task_list`). `target: "story"`
only: the launch's review task links `relates_to:reviews` to it (`fieldSources.reviews:
exact`); without it, a reviewer's task links the story's latest open task
(`associated`).

role.description:
The role to show for the session: `manager`, `worker` or any free
label (`reviewer`, `qa`). Display only; nothing is checked against it.

story_id.description:
The story id to open (e.g. "DEMO-1"). Required for a story target and
resolved trusted-side to its managed worktree; an unknown id or a story
with no worktree yet is refused (the frontend never supplies a path).
With `target: "team-workspace"`, optional:
links the session to that story without changing its context worktree.
Otherwise it inherits its launcher's known story within the same org and team.
Never inferred from names or carried implicitly across teams or orgs.

target.description:
`"story"` or `"team-workspace"`. Absent → the legacy story open (its result
shape is unchanged and the fields below are ignored).

team.description: The team to open in: defaults to your own team for agent sessions, or the active team when a person calls it. With `story`, a team other than the story's is refused.

worktree.description: Context worktree id or name. Pass it whenever the user named one.

tools.name: post_agent_message
tools.description:
Post a progress note to the chat surface bound to your session and to the agent-updates store, available to dashboards through codesense.updates(). Notes do not appear in the native human Inbox. To send the human a report there, use send_message to human with kind update. Fire-and-forget: emits a UI event and returns immediately — for a blocking question, use ask_user instead. Inputs: `sessionId` (your `$CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID`, stamped into your PTY at spawn), `text`. Optional: `role` (default "agent"). The render tripwire may route long or artifact-bearing messages to a doc or artifact pane; pass `subclass` (your Weft subclass: `review`/`research`/`impl`/`planning`) and `hasArtifacts: true` after a report_artifact call for better routing. For a DrillDoc target, `openDocPath` is the absolute context-repo path to open in the viewer (absent → DrillDoc rule skipped).
Docs: arc-e-agents/mcp-only-agents.html

hasArtifacts.description:
Set `true` after calling `report_artifact` so the render
tripwire can annotate the bubble. The server does NOT infer this from
run-store state — the agent is the authoritative source.

openDocPath.description:
The context-repo absolute path to open in the viewer when the
render target resolves to `DrillDoc`. Absent → the DrillDoc rule is
skipped (no blind navigation to an unknown path).

sessionId.description:
The calling session's tab id — pass your `$CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID`
(codesense stamped it into your PTY env at spawn). The UI routes the
message to the chat surface bound to this session.

subclass.description:
The sending worker's Weft subclass (e.g. `"review"`,
`"research"`, `"impl"`, `"planning"`). Feeds the render tripwire — agents
that set it get better routing; omission falls through to length-based
rules.

text.description: The message text to surface in the chat.

tools.name: query_context
tools.description:
Find context files by metadata across synced orgs (team context repos, your private space per org, and all-orgs content). Footprint-wide by default; narrow with `where`. Child callers see only shared ancestor files, even with where.teams. Every arg is optional; `{}` lists the first page of visible files sorted by path.

Rows: { id (story_id or file name), path, relPath, fileName, org (null = all-orgs), team (null = private/all-orgs), layer (team|private|all-orgs), kind (story|bug|spike|epic|doc|dashboard|skill|other), mtime (ms), title, fields (ALL frontmatter / HTML cs:* meta), relationships?, metadataTruncated?, textMatches?: [{title, anchor}] }.

Private items (the user's private space) come back only for ONE org you name: `where.orgs: ["acme"]` (exactly one) or `where.sameOrgAs`. With `orgs: "all"` (the default) or several orgs you get team and all-orgs content only, never private items — and links to private items stay hidden.

Top-level `reviews/` files are excluded by default. To read them deliberately, set `where.pathPrefix` or `where.pathGlob` starting with `reviews/` (for example `reviews/sam/` or `reviews/**/*.md`). Pane queries are unchanged.

- where: { orgs: "all" | ["org"], sameOrgAs: "/abs/path", teams: [..], layers: [..], kinds: [..], pathPrefix: "_bmad-output/13-x" or "/abs", pathGlob: "**/DEMO-*.md" }
- filters: [{ key, op, value | min/max }] — op: eq, in, not, exists, missing, contains (list item or case-insensitive text), range (numeric, or text e.g. ISO dates), prefix. Any frontmatter key or built-in (path, relPath, fileName, id, org, team, layer, kind, mtime, title, dir). Same key → OR; different keys → AND. Value "@me" = the signed-in user.
- match: { status: ["todo","review"], team: "default" } — shorthand (scalar = eq, array = in).
- relationships: { dependsOn, dependedOnBy, hasSupportingDoc, backlinkedBy, parentEpic, hasDeps, isBacklinked } — tokens are a path, story_id, file name or stem.
- text: token-aware full-text across title, headings and body (case-insensitive; reads at most 5,000 files / 64 MB per query after the other filters; textScanTruncated / totalApproximate say when that bound hit).
Text results rank by title coverage, then heading coverage, then body coverage unless sort is explicit. Schema-1 search-index.json sidecars supply optional textMatches anchors on the page row. Only nonempty text queries scoped exactly to where.orgs: ["codesense/docs"] default-exclude generated/ before scanning, reported as excluded: ["generated/"]. Opt in with where.pathPrefix: "generated/" or a pathGlob starting with "generated/". Listings and other orgs are unchanged.

- select: frontmatter keys to return (+ "relationships"); omit for everything. All query field keys accept an optional cs: prefix; topic/task/tools/audience are lists, returned with canonical unprefixed keys.
- sort: ["priority", "-mtime", {key, dir, missing, order}] — status sorts by the built-in workflow order (planning, todo, in-progress, blocked, review, qa, done) unless you pass `order` (e.g. the team's own status list); priority by p0…p4. Values order numbers < dates < text (text naturally: DEMO-9 < DEMO-10). Ties by path.
- eq/in/not compare text exactly ("01" ≠ "1"); pass a JSON number to compare numerically.
- limit (default 200, max 10000), cursor (prior nextCursor, same query; one snapshot per walk, 30 s idle/120 s max, text until a change; then data.code stale_cursor: restart), groupBy: a key → groups [{value, count}] over ALL matches (board columns).

Example — open stories in epic DEMO assigned to me, by priority, as a board:
{"where":{"kinds":["story"]},"relationships":{"parentEpic":"DEMO"},"filters":[{"key":"status","op":"in","value":["todo","in-progress"]},{"key":"assigned_to","op":"eq","value":"@me"}],"sort":["priority"],"groupBy":"status","select":["status","priority"]}

Example — dashboards in one org changed since a date: {"where":{"orgs":["acme"],"kinds":["dashboard"]},"filters":[{"key":"mtime","op":"range","min":1759300000000}],"sort":["-mtime"]}
Docs: arc-k-sync/file-tools.html

filters.description: Filter clauses `[{ key, op, value | min | max }]`; ops: eq, in, not, exists, missing, contains, range, prefix.

groupBy.description: Count matches per value of this key (board columns).

match.description: Shorthand filters `{ key: value | [values] }` (scalar = eq, array = in).

relationships.description: Relationship predicates `{ dependsOn, dependedOnBy, hasSupportingDoc, backlinkedBy, parentEpic, hasDeps, isBacklinked }`.

select.description: Frontmatter keys to return (add "relationships" for refs). Omit for every key.

sort.description: Sort keys: `"status"`, `"-mtime"`, or `{ key, dir: "asc"|"desc", missing: "first"|"last" }`.

text.description: Token-aware title, heading and body match (bounded scan).

where.description: Where to look: `{ orgs: "all" | [slugs], sameOrgAs, teams, layers, kinds, pathPrefix, pathGlob }`.

tools.name: react
tools.description:
React to a message in your inbox with one emoji, like a tapback: the sender and the human see it on the message, and it is not mail (no unread, no wake, no reply). Args: {message_id} (a message you sent, received, or are the reply target of; from read_messages or reply), {emoji} (any single emoji, one character cluster such as 👍, ❤️, 🎉, 🧑🏽‍💻 or a flag; at most 64 bytes; text or two emoji are refused), {remove} (optional boolean: omit it to toggle, true to take your reaction back, false to make sure it is there), {session_id} (optional: omit it to use this connection's verified tab identity). One reaction per (you, message, emoji): reacting again with the same emoji toggles it off, so to keep it pass {remove:false}. The message's sender hears of a new reaction once, in a `reactions` list next to `messages` the next time it calls read_messages. A message you are not a party to (for example mail between two other agents) answers `no message`. Returns `{status:"reacted",messageId,emoji,outcome:"added"|"removed"|"unchanged"}` or `{status:"invalid",message}`. Example: react {message_id: 42, emoji: "👍"}.
Docs: arc-f-inboxes-and-triage/messages.html

emoji.description: Exactly one emoji (one character cluster, at most 64 bytes).

message_id.description: The message to react to, from `read_messages` or `reply`.

remove.description: Omit to toggle; `true` takes your reaction back; `false` makes sure it is there.

session_id.description:
Omit to react as this connection's verified tab. If supplied, it must name that
same tab. An unbound connection is refused.

tools.name: read_content_file
tools.description:
Read content file by path. Reads use the calling session's team: ancestor files must be shared with that child, even for an absolute parent path. Private content retains its existing scope. Returns {text?, bytesUrl?, size, truncated, sha256}. maxBytes is capped at 1.5 MB; bytesUrl streams large or binary files through /viewer. This is the MCP twin of files.read.
Docs: arc-k-sync/file-tools.html

tools.name: read_messages
tools.description:
Drain your unread inbox messages (oldest first; each returned once then marked read). Inbox mail comes from people and agents that your user's setup lets reach you, so anyone who can message you is someone your user trusts. Call this when your hook tells you "You have N new messages. Call read_messages with session_id <id>." — pass that id as {session_id} (your $CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID), or omit it to read the inbox of the tab this MCP connection runs in. A hand-started CLI in a CodeSense terminal is bound to that tab. An outside or unbound connection is refused; start the CLI in a CodeSense terminal. A supplied session_id must name this same tab. Returns `{messages: [{messageId, from, fromName, text, inReplyTo, inReplyToTeam, replyTo?, summary?, primaryFile?, attachmentHint?}]}`; `summary` is the sender's one-line plain-text preview of `text`, when it set one; `replyTo` (when the sender set one) is where your reply goes instead of to the sender; `primaryFile` is a logical path the sender attached, and when `attachmentHint` is present an agent whose workspace lacks the file can call `hydrate_story` with `attachmentHint.owningStoryId` to copy it in. Answer any one with reply, or acknowledge it with react. When someone reacted to a message you sent, the result also has `reactions: [{messageId, emoji, reactor, createdAtMs, team: {org, team}}]` (`team` names the team that holds the message, which matters when you mailed an agent in another team), each new reaction reported once (a reaction taken back before you read it is never reported); reactions are not mail and are never counted as unread.
Docs: arc-f-inboxes-and-triage/messages.html

session_id.description:
Your `$CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID`; omit it to read the inbox of the tab this MCP
connection runs in. An unbound connection is refused; start the CLI in a CodeSense terminal.

tools.name: records_create
tools.description:
Records create: operate on a declared Markdown folder collection through the shared records core. Org and team default to the session context. At most 64 fields per call. Private collections have local git history; team and story collections do not. Identity comes from the verified MCP connection; an unbound caller is refused. A supplied sessionId must name the caller itself.
Docs: arc-i-dashboard-primitives/records.html

org.description: Org containing the collection; defaults to the session's org.

patch.description: Edits to apply to the record's body, as a JSON value.

sessionId.description: Identity comes from the verified connection; a supplied id must name the same caller.

team.description: Team for a shared collection; defaults to the session's team.

tools.name: records_list
tools.description:
Records list: operate on a declared Markdown folder collection through the shared records core. Org and team default to the session context. Private collections have local git history; team and story collections do not. Identity comes from the verified MCP connection; an unbound caller is refused. A supplied sessionId must name the caller itself.
Docs: arc-i-dashboard-primitives/records.html

org.description: Org containing the collection; defaults to the session's org.

patch.description: Edits to apply to the record's body, as a JSON value.

sessionId.description: Identity comes from the verified connection; a supplied id must name the same caller.

team.description: Team for a shared collection; defaults to the session's team.

tools.name: remove_source_repo
tools.description:
Remove a source repo from a team: the team stops tracking it, and when no team in any of your orgs still tracks it, the record binding its local clone is forgotten. The clone itself stays on disk, untouched. Pass `org`, `team` and `repo` (owner/repo or host/owner/repo). Returns { status:"ok", data:{ remoteKey, unboundClone } } where `unboundClone` is the clone whose binding was forgotten (still on disk), or null when none was bound or another team still uses it; an unknown team returns { status:"unauthorizedTeam" }; a repo the team does not track returns { status:"validation", message }.
Docs: arc-k-sync/moving-between-contexts.html

repo.description: One of the team's source repos: `owner/repo` or `host/owner/repo`.

tools.name: reply
tools.description:
Optional {requestId} deduplicates retries: send the same key and payload after a disconnect to return the original messageId; a changed payload is refused. Omit it to create a new message. Reply to an inbox message — delivered like send_message to whoever sent the original (agent or human), or, when the original carries a `replyTo`, ONLY to that address instead (email Reply-To): a session's inbox, the human, or for `role:<id>` a pending delivery in that role's queue that any instance of the role claims later, even after the original sender exited. Args: {message_id} (from read_messages), {text}, {session_id} (optional: omit it to answer as this connection's verified tab; if supplied it must name that same tab; an unbound connection is refused (start the CLI in a CodeSense terminal), never answered as the human; the reply shows as the sender's current tab name, see who_am_i). Optional {media:{url|path,alt}} attaches a GIF or image; alt is required. Reply body renders as markdown by default. {summary} is one plain-text line (≤280 chars) shown as this reply's preview in lists; set it when the body is long or heavily formatted. {kind} "needs-you" | "update": what a reply to the human asks of them, as in send_message; omitted, a reply is an "update" (the human is waiting on your answer, not you on theirs) — pass "needs-you" when your reply asks them something back. A reply queued for a role keeps no kind. Returns `{status:"sent",messageId,kind?,hint?}` (`kind` and `hint` as for send_message, for a reply to the human) or `{status:"invalid",message}` (blank text without media / unknown message id / a sessionId that is not running).
Docs: arc-f-inboxes-and-triage/index.html

anyOf.description:
What a message asks of the human, for agent views and dashboards. The human
inbox shows both kinds as conversations and counts all unread human mail. Stored as given on `wv_inbox.kind` (NULL when the sender set none); reads
resolve the effective kind with [`InboxMessage::effective_kind`].

oneOf.description: Waits on the human: a question, a decision, something only they can unblock.

kind.description:
What a reply to the human asks of them: `"needs-you"` when it asks them
something back, else `"update"` (the default for a reply). A reply queued for a
role keeps no kind.

media.description: Optional GIF or image: exactly one of HTTPS url or local path, and required alt text.

requestId.description: Retry key: reuse the same value and payload after a transport disconnect.

session_id.description:
Omit to answer as this connection's verified tab. If supplied, it must name
that same tab. An unbound connection is refused; start the CLI in a CodeSense
terminal. Only the native app can answer as the person.

summary.description:
One plain-text line (≤280 chars) shown as this reply's preview in lists; set it
when the body is long or heavily formatted.

tools.name: routine_arm_on
tools.description:
Routine arm on — move where a routine fires: `machine:"this_mac"` (this Mac fires it, as "Run on this Mac" does) or a machine id from list_machines (that machine's terminal server fires it on its own clock, in the routine's zone, whether or not any Mac is open; this Mac manages it: it prepares the agent there now and on every edit, pushes the routine's definition whenever it reconnects, and records its runs; later changes to the agent's own files reach the machine only through routine_refresh_on_machine). A routine armed on a machine runs on its schedule only (no agent_done, inbox_idle or role_pending triggers), once for the team, with its agent on that machine. Each move is a new revision under a new arm epoch: the machine refuses anything older, so a stale definition never re-arms it. Moving it off a machine waits for that machine to acknowledge before anything else fires it (`handover_pending`), so a move never doubles a fire. Required: `id`, `machine`. Optional: `sessionId` (omitted, the verified connection; if supplied, the same caller only). Counts against the 25 enabled-routine cap. Returns { status:"ok", data:{ id, armed_machine, arm_epoch, revision, handover_pending, machine_warning? } } (`machine_warning`: armed, but not prepared on the machine yet, and why: not connected, preparation failed or still running, or waiting on the machine it moved off), or `validation`. Identity comes from the verified MCP connection; an unbound caller is refused. A supplied sessionId must name the caller itself.
Docs: arc-g-routines/routine-yml.html

machine.description:
`this_mac`: this Mac fires it. A machine id (from list_machines): that
machine's terminal server fires it on its own clock, with or without
this Mac.

sessionId.description: Omit to use the verified connection identity. A supplied id must name that caller.

tools.name: routine_create
tools.description:
Create a routine. For something only for your current session, use schedule_wakeup. Each fire runs `task` on `agent` per `mode`, with history. `task` is the agent's whole prompt: CodeSense adds nothing to it. It may use `{{date}}`, `{{timestamp}}`, `{{last_run_at}}` (empty on the first run), `{{last_run_summary}}` (the last successful `signal_done` summary) and declared `{{variables}}`. `task` is the whole contract: a run ends when the agent process exits, when it calls `signal_done`, or at `maxRuntime`. For a result or question, instruct `signal_done` with `summary` or status `needs-attention` and the question; otherwise the run simply ends. A `visible` agent stays open after work; without that call its run lasts until the user closes the tab or `maxRuntime`. Meanwhile fires follow `overlap`. For a structured result, declare `resultSchema` and have the task call routine_publish_result, then signal_done success. Headless Claude may call `routine_context` / `routine_publish_result` only when `permissions.claude.allow` lists them (as `mcp__codesense__<tool>`; `signal_done` always works). Routines never deliver results: to send, post or file something, the task must name the tool, and the agent needs that server in `mcpServers`. Example: `{"name":"Triage","when":"weekdays 09:00","agent":"triage","task":"Read mail, then signal_done with a summary."}`. Unsure? Pass `dryRun:true` first. Wake limits: maxWakes, maxWakesPerDay, minGap (mode wake only). Creation is a local context-repo edit that notifies no one, shown under its agent in Agents | Schedule; sharing needs a git push. An each_mac recipe is off until enabled on each Mac. Returns { status:"ok", data:{ id, agent, agent_key, mode, effective_mode, schedule_in_words, next_fires:[next 3, RFC3339; empty for a draft], enabled, revision, warnings:[{code, message}], deprecations? } }: `warnings` never block the save (e.g. a `/name` task missing from the agent's `startup`; fix with agent_update). Or validation, unauthorizedTeam, notSyncedLocally. Events use the YAML model: events:[{kind:"inbox_idle"}] fires on idle sessions with unread mail; events:[{kind:"agent_done",from_agent:"reviewer"}] watches that agent finishing (omit from_agent for all in reach). Use events:[{kind:"role_pending"}] to watch every queue in reach. Use events:[{kind:"role_pending",role:"reviewer"}] to watch only reviewer mail. role must be nonblank and is valid only for role_pending; from_agent only for agent_done. No role or from_agent existence check. Omitted/null events keeps current events; [] clears these three kinds; nonempty replaces only them, preserving schedules and metadata triggers. Event errors return status:validation with events[i].field and a hint. These events support each_mac; machine arming restrictions still apply. metadataTriggers takes query_context selection, target eq and optional previous eq for a transition. Existing matches baseline at discovery/restart. [] clears metadata triggers; omitted/null keeps them. Metadata triggers require one_mac. Recipients use routine_context and the wake header runId. action:command runs command:[program,arg,...] directly without an agent/model; rendered argv is returned. Commands are team/local only, default overlap queue/maxRuntime 5m. Bare executables use PATH; relative executable paths must stay inside the team content root; absolute executable paths are refused. Exit 0 succeeds; routine_run exposes bounded, secret-redacted output (last 4 KB). after:{routine:id,on:succeeded|finished} chains in the same space; finished excludes cancelled/skipped/coalesced, cycles and missing upstream are refused. after:null clears on update. budgetUsd {perDay?,perWeek?} is fresh-agent only; raising/removing a cap needs native Accept. dryRun:true validates resolved triggers and rendered argv without writing a definition. Verified caller required; sessionId must match.
Docs: arc-g-routines/trigger-cookbook.html

action.description:
agent (default) or command. action:command takes command:[program,arg,...]
instead of agent/task/mode; it runs as you, with no agent or model, in a
team workspace or managed repo clone. Defaults: overlap queue, maxRuntime 5m.
Only me and machine-armed command routines are refused.

after.description:
Fire after a routine in the same space succeeds or finishes. `finished`
excludes cancelled/skipped/coalesced. Cycles and missing upstream routines
are refused. Chained fires carry trigger.{run_id,routine,phase,result_text,detail}.

agent.description:
The agent the routine belongs to and runs: its `id` from agent_list in the
routine's own space (a bare `triage` is the team's agent for a team
routine and your private agent for an Only me one), or its full key, which
lets an Only me routine run a team agent. A team routine needs an agent of
its own team or a starter (`builtin/claude`, `builtin/codex`), since any
teammate's Mac may run it. Required, unless `sessionId` names a session
launched as a saved agent (then that one; a session launched as a starter
still defaults to that starter, with a `deprecations` note). The routine
lives under it, in `config/agents/<agent>/routines/<id>/`; each run
launches it with the running user's own account at its current revision,
archived or not.
The reply names the one chosen; routine_update changes it.

budgetUsd.description:
budgetUsd {perDay?,perWeek?}: positive finite USD; local calendar day and
Monday-start week, not rolling windows. Fresh only: wakes cap the agent;
commands cannot. Machine-armed caps are refused. Raising/removing a cap
needs native Accept; lowering ratchets the local accepted ceiling.
Unrestricted shells are trusted; sandbox untrusted agents.

command.description:
Program and arguments, one entry each. A bare program uses PATH; a relative
executable path must be executable inside the team content root; absolute
executable paths are refused. Args render individually, never through a shell.
Exit 0 succeeds; routine_run exposes the secret-redacted last 4 KB of output.

enabled.description:
Whether it fires from this Mac. Default true (false for a draft that
never fires until routine_set_enabled resumes it); for `runsOn:
each_mac`, default false, and true turns it on for this Mac.
The 25 enabled-routine cap is checked when enabling.

events.description:
Events: [{"kind":"inbox_idle"}], [{"kind":"agent_done","from_agent":"reviewer"}],
or [{"kind":"role_pending","role":"reviewer"}]. Omit role for every queue in reach.

items.description: Event inputs share the YAML model's spelling and validation.

from_agent.description: agent_done only: agent id or full key; omitted watches all agents in reach.

role.description: role_pending only: nonempty queue name; omitted watches every queue in reach.

id.description: The routine id within its team. Default: derived from `name`; a taken id is validation.

machine.description:
Where a wake looks for (and starts) the agent: `local` (default, this
Mac), a machine id from list_machines, or `any` connected machine (wakes
the agent wherever it runs, starts it here when none does). With
`runsOn: each_mac` it must be `local`, except that a `fresh` routine may
use `any`. A session on an offline machine still counts as running, so
that wake is undelivered (machine_offline) and nothing starts.

maxRuntime.description: How long one run may take, like `30m` or `2h`. Default `30m`.

maxWakes.description:
Optional: how many wakes this routine may deliver in all. Reached, it
pauses itself and posts one inbox note; resuming starts a new count.
Light checks need no wake limits; heavy work may use
"minGap":"4h","maxWakesPerDay":3,"overlap":"skip".
Past 120 wakes/hour per session, wakes return rate_limited (one inbox note).
Omit for no limit. Wake limits count wakes typed into a live session, so
they apply to `mode: wake` only (a `fresh` routine with limits saves with
a `wake_limits_ignored` warning; a start when none runs is not counted).
The terminal server running the session enforces them, so they hold
with the desktop closed; each Mac and machine keeps its own count, and
a machine whose terminal server is too old is sent no limited wake
(undelivered (unavailable), with one inbox note to update it).

maxWakesPerDay.description:
Optional: wakes in any rolling 24 h. Fires over it are
`undelivered(limit_reached)` and it resumes on its own. A wake limit
(see `maxWakes`): `mode: wake` only.

metadataTriggers.description:
Metadata conditions using query_context's selection and eq clauses. Example:
[{"selection":{"where":{"kinds":["story"]}},"target":{"key":"status","op":"eq","value":"in-progress"}}].
Add previous:{"key":"status","op":"eq","value":"planning"} for an exact transition.
Matches at first discovery or restart are a baseline; only later entry fires.
Omit to preserve; [] removes metadata triggers on update, keeping other events.
Not with runsOn:each_mac. Recipients read changes with routine_context and
the wake header runId (incl. coalesced_payloads).

minGap.description:
Optional: the least time between two wakes of this routine (into any
session) (`30m`, `2h`, `1d`; at most `7d`), for wakes that start heavy
work. A fire inside it is coalesced or skipped per `overlap`. A wake
limit (see `maxWakes`): `mode: wake` only.

missed.description:
`skip` (default) or `run_once`: what happens to fires missed while the
app was closed or asleep.

mode.description:
`wake` (deliver the task into the agent's live session when it is
idle, starting one with `task` as its first prompt only when none runs;
never a second instance) or `fresh` ("start a new" in the app: a new
instance in `where` on each fire, headless unless `visible`). Omitted: `wake` for a visible routine on a
saved agent that launches in a tab, else `fresh`; the reply's
`effective_mode` says what a fire does. A built-in starter's routines
are fresh only.

name.description: What the routine is called, e.g. "Morning triage".

overlap.description:
`coalesce` (default), `skip` or `queue`: what a fire does while a run is
still going.

resultSchema.description:
Optional bounded inline JSON Schema for the routine's private dashboard
result; omit when no structured result is required.

runsOn.description:
A team routine only: `one_mac` (default) runs it once for the team, on
this Mac until moved (a shared job, e.g. a bug bot or team triage); `each_mac` makes
it a recipe each teammate turns on for their own Mac (e.g. a digest or a
reminder for oneself), off everywhere until they do, with its own runs
on each.

scope.description:
`team` (default: teammates can see it) or `personal` (Only me, only when
the user asks for it: your private space for `org`, which is then
required and must be an org synced on this Mac; it runs in that org
only). A team routine goes in `org`/`team`, or the active team when both
are omitted. Anyone who sees it can change it; `owner` grants nothing.

sessionId.description: Omit to use the verified connection identity. A supplied id must name that caller.

task.description:
What the agent should do on each run, in plain words. Example:
"Summarize acme/web issues since {{last_run_at}} to #web-triage with Slack
MCP tools, then signal_done with it."

tz.description: The IANA zone `when` is read in. Default: this machine's zone.

variables.description:
Task variables, `{ name: { type, default } }`, referenced as `{{name}}`:
e.g. `{"channel": {"type": "text", "default": "#web"}}` used as
`{{channel}}`.

visible.description: Run in a visible terminal tab instead of headless. Default false.

when.description:
When it runs, read in `tz`: a preset (`every 5m|10m|15m|20m|30m`,
`every 1h|2h|3h|4h|6h|8h|12h`, `hourly`, `daily 09:00`, `weekdays 08:30`,
`weekly mon 17:00`, on a 24-hour clock) or a 5-field cron such as
`0 9 * * 1-5`. Nothing fires more often than every 5 minutes. Omit it for a
routine that runs only when started by hand. Empty when removes schedules;
other event triggers are kept.

tools.name: routine_delete
tools.description:
Routine delete — archive any routine you can see: it stops firing and leaves routine_list, and its run history stays readable. Required: `id`. Optional: `sessionId` (optional: omitted, the verified connection; if supplied, the same caller only). Any routine you can see is yours to change, a teammate's included: the change is a local edit to the context repo, and sharing it with the team is a git push your agent makes. Notifies no one. Returns { status:"ok", data:{ id, archived:true, revision } }, or `validation`. Identity comes from the verified MCP connection; an unbound caller is refused. A supplied sessionId must name the caller itself.
Docs: arc-g-routines/routine-yml.html

sessionId.description: Omit to use the verified connection identity. A supplied id must name that caller.

tools.name: routine_list
tools.description:
Routine list — every routine you can see: your Only me ones (in your private space for the open org) and those of every team synced on this Mac, yours and teammates', all of which you can change. Optional `agent` (an agent's `id` or key from agent_list): only that agent's routines. Returns { status:"ok", data:[{ id, scope, org, team, name, schedule_in_words, agent, agent_key, unassigned (its agent is nowhere on this Mac: it never fires until routine_update gives it one), duplicate (another routine of its space has its id: it never fires), mode, effective_mode, where, runs_on, enabled, next_run_at, last_run:{status, reason, at}|null, owner, owner_name, created_by, armed_here, needs_you, revision, content_stale? }] }. `content_stale` ({ machine, since_ms, why }) marks a routine armed on a machine whose prepared content is behind it: the machine starts its agent from what was prepared before until routine_refresh_on_machine. Times are RFC3339. `runs_on` is `one_mac` (a shared job: it runs on exactly one Mac, and `armed_here` says it is this one; one written by hand that names no Mac runs nowhere, `armed_here` false and `next_run_at` null, until a save here places it on this Mac) or `each_mac` (a recipe each Mac runs: `enabled` says whether it is on for this Mac). `enabled`, `next_run_at`, `last_run` and `needs_you` are this Mac's. `id` is what every other routine tool takes; `revision` is routine_update's `baseRevision`.
Docs: arc-g-routines/index.html

agent.description: Only the routines of this agent: its `id` or key from agent_list.

tools.name: routine_run
tools.description:
Routine run — one routine run in full, by id. Required: `runId` (a `run_id` from routine_runs, routine_get's `runs`, or routine_list's `last_run`). Returns { status:"ok", data:{ routine_id, routine_name, run_id, revision, source, phase, reason, linked_run_id, created_at, started_at, ended_at, result_text, detail, agent } }: the routine_runs row plus the routine it belongs to (`routine_id` is what routine_get takes); `detail` explains why it ended, as in routine_runs. `phase`: `queued` | `running` | `succeeded` | `failed` | `needs_you` (it ended asking you something; `result_text` is the question) | `ended` (its agent exited without signal_done) | `timed_out` | `cancelled` | `skipped` (did not run; `reason` says why) | `coalesced` (folded into `linked_run_id`). `source`: what fired it (`schedule`, `manual`, an event). Times are RFC3339. A run of a routine you cannot see is `validation`.
Docs: arc-g-routines/index.html

runId.description:
A routine run's `run_id` (from routine_runs, routine_get's `runs`, or
routine_list's `last_run`).

tools.name: routine_run_now
tools.description:
Routine run now — fire any routine you can see once, by hand, on this Mac, through its own policy: a paused routine records a skip, and a run still going makes this fire coalesce, skip or wait per its `overlap`. Required: `id`. Optional: `variables` ({name: value} for its declared variables); `sessionId` (optional: omitted, the verified connection; if supplied, the same caller only). Returns { status:"ok", data:{ run_id, outcome } }, where outcome is `queued` (with `reason:"held"` when it waits behind the run still going), `coalesced` (with `active_run_id`), `skipped:<reason>`, or `duplicate` (this fire already has a run); or `validation`. Follow the run with routine_runs. Identity comes from the verified MCP connection; an unbound caller is refused. A supplied sessionId must name the caller itself.
Docs: arc-g-routines/index.html

sessionId.description: Omit to use the verified connection identity. A supplied id must name that caller.

variables.description: Values for the routine's declared variables.

tools.name: routine_set_enabled
tools.description:
Routine set enabled — pause (`enabled:false`) or resume (`enabled:true`) any routine you can see. It changes only whether it fires from this Mac; the definition is untouched, so it is never a git change. A paused routine is a draft. For an `each_mac` routine this is "Run on my Mac": `true` turns it on for this Mac, `false` off. A shared job armed on another Mac (`armed_here` false) fires and is paused there; pausing it here changes nothing until it is moved to this Mac. Required: `id`, `enabled`. Optional: `sessionId` (optional: omitted, the verified connection; if supplied, the same caller only). Resuming counts against the 25 enabled-routine cap. Resuming a routine armed on a machine prepares it there. Returns { status:"ok", data:{ id, enabled, machine_warning? } } (`machine_warning`: resumed, but not prepared on its machine, and why), or `validation`. Identity comes from the verified MCP connection; an unbound caller is refused. A supplied sessionId must name the caller itself.
Docs: arc-g-routines/index.html

enabled.description:
false pauses it on this machine (turns an `each_mac` routine off for
this Mac); true resumes it (turns it on).

sessionId.description: Omit to use the verified connection identity. A supplied id must name that caller.

The agent uses prior prepared content until preparation succeeds; routine_refresh_on_machine retries); { status:"conflict", data:{ message, current_revision } } when it changed since `baseRevision` (nothing was changed: routine_get it again and reapply); or `validation`. Events use the YAML model: events:[{kind:"inbox_idle"}] fires on idle sessions with unread mail; events:[{kind:"agent_done",from_agent:"reviewer"}] watches that agent finishing (omit from_agent for all in reach). Use events:[{kind:"role_pending"}] to watch every queue in reach. Use events:[{kind:"role_pending",role:"reviewer"}] to watch only reviewer mail. role must be nonblank and is valid only for role_pending; from_agent only for agent_done. No role or from_agent existence check. Omitted/null events keeps current events; [] clears these three kinds; nonempty replaces only them, preserving schedules and metadata triggers. Event errors return status:validation with events[i].field and a hint. These events support each_mac; machine arming restrictions still apply. metadataTriggers takes query_context selection, target eq and optional previous eq for a transition. Existing matches baseline at discovery/restart. [] clears metadata triggers; omitted/null keeps them. Metadata triggers require one_mac. Recipients use routine_context and the wake header runId. action:command runs command:[program,arg,...] directly without an agent/model; rendered argv is returned. Commands are team/local only, default overlap queue/maxRuntime 5m. Bare executables use PATH; relative executable paths must stay inside the team content root; absolute executable paths are refused. Exit 0 succeeds; routine_run exposes bounded, secret-redacted output (last 4 KB). after:{routine:id,on:succeeded|finished} chains in the same space; finished excludes cancelled/skipped/coalesced, cycles and missing upstream are refused. after:null clears on update. budgetUsd {perDay?,perWeek?} is fresh-agent only; raising/removing a cap needs native Accept. Verified caller required; sessionId must match.
Docs: arc-g-routines/trigger-cookbook.html

action.description:
agent (default) or command. action:command takes command:[program,arg,...]
instead of agent/task/mode; it runs as you, with no agent or model, in a
team workspace or managed repo clone. Defaults: overlap queue, maxRuntime 5m.
Only me and machine-armed command routines are refused.

after.description:
Fire after a routine in the same space succeeds or finishes. `finished`
excludes cancelled/skipped/coalesced. Cycles and missing upstream routines
are refused. Chained fires carry trigger.{run_id,routine,phase,result_text,detail}.
